summary: The paper proposes a VQ-VAE + mutual-information pipeline to characterize planning behaviors (horizon, branch awareness, layer/block information distribution) in decoder-only LMs, comparing next-token vs. multi-token training on CFG, path-finding, and OpenWebText. The methodology is reasonable and the questions are interesting, but the scientific yield is modest: the main empirical findings are that planning is task-dependent, MTP differs only 'modestly' from NTP, and recent computations dominate — most of which will strike ICLR readers as expected. Scope is narrow (small in-house GPT-3-Small–style models on two toy tasks plus OpenWebText; no off-the-shelf pretrained model), and the MI numbers hinge on VQ-VAE choices whose sensitivity is only partly probed. The framework is worth developing, but current claims and evidence sit below the ICLR bar without additional analysis and stronger validation.
strengths: Well-motivated framing: planning as horizon + branch awareness, connected to MPC / world-model literature and to the debate on probing vs. information-theoretic tools.

The VQ-VAE + MI pipeline is an interesting alternative to probing that (as argued in App. D.2) avoids conflating probe capacity with representation content, and it is applied consistently across three qualitatively different datasets.
The branch-awareness experiment with disjoint alternative and decoy paths (Table 1) is a clean design that rules out trivial token overlap as an explanation.
The layer/block diagnostic (Fig. 4) including the conditional nMI control that isolates position T's contribution is a nice methodological touch that goes beyond a plain heatmap.
Calibration is generally careful: the authors explicitly restrict claims to relative, within-setting comparisons of nMI rather than absolute MI values.

key_concerns.issue: Experimental scope is too narrow for the generality suggested by the title and abstract. All main results use custom-trained GPT-3-Small–scale models on CFG, PF, and OpenWebText; there are no experiments on pretrained open LMs (GPT-2 family, Pythia, Llama, Qwen, etc.), no systematic scaling beyond a single 0.3B appendix point, and no natural-language reasoning tasks (GSM8K-style, code, planning benchmarks). Claims about 'planning in LMs' and about NTP-vs-MTP effects therefore rest on a very thin experimental base.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add at least one family of pretrained open-source LMs at ≥2 scales and one reasoning-oriented natural language task; report how horizon/branch/recency findings vary with scale and pretraining regime.

key_concerns.issue: The MI estimates depend critically on the VQ-VAE (codebook size K, encoder capacity, entropy/cosine regularizers, training data), and different VQ-VAEs are trained for different experiments. This makes it hard to know whether observed differences (e.g., CFG's fast decay vs. PF-Long's slower decay, or MTP vs. NTP contrasts) reflect the LM's computation or the compressor. The sensitivity study in App. A.4 is invoked but not shown here; the reader cannot assess robustness.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report nMI curves and the main qualitative conclusions across a grid of K (e.g., 128/512/2048), encoder depths, and loss weights, and show that within-setting orderings (which is what the paper claims) are stable. Also test an alternative compressor (e.g., k-means on PCA-reduced states) as a control.

key_concerns.issue: Statistical evidence is thin. Fig. 3's captions describe nMI vs. τ curves but do not indicate seeds/error bars; Table 1 reports mean ± std but the numbers (e.g., MNTP PF-Long accuracy 0.60 ± 0.01 vs. MMTP 0.85 ± 0.02, and I(ZH;Zalt)/I(ZH;Zdecoy) contrasts) beg for significance tests and n. The qualitative NTP-vs-MTP conclusions (framed as 'no consistent differences' in the conclusion but 'modestly reduces myopic behavior' earlier) are also inconsistent.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report seeds (≥3–5), error bars/CIs on all nMI curves in Fig. 3 and Fig. 4, and paired significance tests for NTP vs. MTP comparisons. Reconcile the abstract/§3.1 vs. conclusion wording on MTP effects.

key_concerns.issue: The core empirical findings are largely unsurprising given prior work: (a) short-range decay of prefix→future MI on locally syntactic data and longer-range structure on planning tasks is essentially expected; (b) 'recent tokens and late layers carry the most next-token information' has been reported repeatedly (e.g., logit-lens / tuned-lens, Pal et al.'s future-token results); (c) branch awareness on tasks with two constructed solutions is interesting but tightly tied to how the alternative and decoy are generated. The delta over prior work needs to be argued more sharply.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Explicitly enumerate what is quantitatively new relative to Pal et al. (2023), Shai et al. (2024), and future-token probing; ideally reproduce one of their findings with your pipeline and show a novel prediction it makes that probing cannot.

key_concerns.issue: The critique of probing vs. MI is central to the paper's methodological contribution but is not established in the main text — it is deferred to App. D.2. Given that Voita & Titov and others have already made this point, the paper needs a crisp demonstration in the body that its MI-based conclusions would differ (qualitatively) from what a probing-based analysis would report on the same data.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Move a compact head-to-head experiment into §2 or §3 showing a concrete case where probing and MI disagree, with an argument for why MI is closer to ground truth.

key_concerns.issue: Normalized MI is only comparable within a single experimental setting because Imax is defined per analysis, yet the discussion sometimes reads as cross-task ('CFG decays quickly; PF stays high'). This is defensible but should be more carefully hedged.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a paragraph in §2 clarifying exactly which cross-plot comparisons are and are not meaningful, and rephrase any cross-task claims that rely on absolute nMI magnitude.

key_concerns.issue: Presentation issues: multiple missing spaces and broken word-boundaries throughout the extracted text (likely PDF-to-text artifacts, but also present in submitted equations/inline math), unnumbered sections, an unclear inline math rendering in §2 (r_S, e_k) and the objective, and Figure 2 caption blending three panels. This will hurt readability at reviewer time.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Clean up typography, add proper section numbering, and split Fig. 2 into clearly labeled subfigures.

key_concerns.issue: 'Planning' is used broadly and sometimes as a term of art (MPC), sometimes as MI-based diagnostic. Given the strong framing (title, abstract, intro), readers may over-interpret MI patterns as evidence of algorithmic planning rather than statistical predictive dependence.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Weaken the framing to 'predictive dependence' or 'planning-like structure', and reserve 'planning' for behaviorally verified cases; or add a behavioral corroboration for at least one MI-based claim.

questions_for_authors: How sensitive are the main qualitative conclusions (CFG rapid decay, PF-Long sustained nMI, NTP-vs-MTP contrasts, branch-awareness ratio > 1) to codebook size K, VQ-VAE depth, and the cosine/entropy regularization weights? Please show a sensitivity grid in the main text.

Do results replicate on any pretrained open LM (e.g., GPT-2, Pythia, Llama) on OpenWebText, or on a reasoning benchmark like GSM8K or CoinFlip? If not, why should readers expect the CFG/PF findings to generalize?

The conclusion states 'no consistent differences between NTP- and MTP-trained models', but §3.1 says MTP 'modestly reduces myopic behavior' and Table 1 shows a sizable accuracy gap on PF-Long. Which claim is correct, and what significance tests support it?

How is I_max chosen for the branch-awareness ratio in Table 1 (raw MI is reported, not nMI), and what null distribution should one expect for I(Z_H;Z_alt)/I(Z_H;Z_decoy) given the construction of alternative/decoy paths? Have you tested a permutation baseline where 'alt' is swapped with a genuinely random correct-length path?

The conditional nMI(Z^ℓ_{T-15:T-1}; Z^L_T | Z^ℓ_T) ≈ 0.3 (Fig. 4 right) is the paper's cleanest claim, but its interpretation depends on the joint code space size and estimator bias. Can you show the finite-sample bias analysis of App. E applied specifically to this quantity?

Given the criticisms of probing you make in §2, can you provide a direct head-to-head where probing and your MI method give qualitatively different answers on the same LM, with an argument for which is closer to a ground truth?
calibration_check: Claims are mostly scoped appropriately to relative within-setting nMI comparisons, but the framing ('planning in LMs', title-level generality) and the inconsistent NTP-vs-MTP wording between §3 and the conclusion overstate what the small-model, three-task evidence actually supports.

significance.justification: Interesting angle on an important question, but headline findings (task-dependence, recency, weak NTP/MTP gap) are largely expected and unlikely to change practice without stronger, larger-scale evidence.

novelty.justification: VQ-VAE-summarized MI over hidden-state blocks is a reasonable combination but the individual components (VQ-VAE, MI-based interpretability, future-token analysis, layer localization) are well-established; the delta over Pal et al., Shai et al., and information-theoretic probing critiques is incremental.

rigor.justification: The pipeline is coherent and the conditional-nMI control in §3.3 is thoughtful, but MI estimates depend on VQ-VAE choices that are only partly examined, and the estimator's bias analysis is deferred to the appendix without being applied to the headline numbers.

statistical_soundness.justification: Multiple seeds are mentioned and Table 1 shows mean±std, but Fig. 3/4 captions do not indicate error bars, no significance tests are reported for NTP vs. MTP contrasts, and the conclusion's 'no consistent differences' is not statistically substantiated.

calibration_honesty.justification: Authors explicitly restrict interpretation of nMI to relative comparisons and note limits of coarse-graining, but §3 and the conclusion give inconsistent messages on the MTP effect, and the title/framing over-reaches beyond the small-model, toy-task evidence base.

clarity.justification: Structure is standard and the core ideas are communicable, but the prose is dense, math notation is uneven, key methodological details and validations live in the appendix, and the extracted text shows many broken word boundaries and equation-formatting issues that will hurt readers.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard Abstract/Intro/Related/Method/Experiments/Conclusion layout at typical ICLR length; related work is present in body prose even without a reference list, and section numbering is somewhat garbled but interpretable.

reproducibility.justification: Model architecture (GPT-3 Small-like), datasets (CFG, PF, OpenWebText), losses, and VQ-VAE objective are described at a level that could be reimplemented, but many crucial hyperparameters (codebook size K, encoder capacity, λ_q/λ_cos/λ_ent, MTP head configuration) are relegated to appendices summarized in captions.

related_work.justification: Reasonable coverage of mechanistic interpretability, probing, and information-theoretic critiques; however, the delineation from Pal et al. and future-token probing is not sharp enough, and the strong critiques of probing are asserted more than demonstrated in the main body.

figure_quality.justification: Captions describe informative comparisons (nMI vs. τ, block/layer heatmaps, conditional-nMI panel), but the panels appear to lack visible error bars and Fig. 2's tri-panel design is over-loaded; the display items support the claims adequately but do not go beyond that.

breadth_generality.justification: Only small in-house GPT-3-Small-scale models on two synthetic tasks plus OpenWebText; no pretrained open LMs, no reasoning benchmarks, and only a single 0.3B appendix scaling point. The generality of the framing ('planning in LMs') is under-supported.

overall_recommendation.justification: Interesting framework and some clean design choices, but narrow experimental scope, methodologically-load-bearing VQ-VAE choices that are not adequately stress-tested, weak statistical reporting, and largely-expected findings put this below the ICLR acceptance bar as submitted.
